Content: Which US and Canada companies are missing from German's lists and should use Yuno to improve operational efficiency. Built 27-Oct-2026.

NorthAm Focus List 2026 workbook (Core ICP 255, Northam ICP 1,488, 2027 Core ICP 100, Gaming, Priorities Top Gaming, General Pipe and Active Pipe Sync Magdalena, Pipe Samuel, SF BDs, BNB MTZ, WorldPay outage, Lost Opps, New Products tabs); German's Master workbook (Master 207, Master Leads, AI Oct 7, Revenue unverified, Yuno customers removed, Non-US removed); TCL (666 and 681 rows); Target Accounts NORAM Team; Yuno ICP Bank; AI Prospects Master; SF AI Prospects; airlines lists; the five 2026 research banks (yuno_icp_combined 868, master bank 727, US priority 252, B2C US 172, mid-market 210).

Names normalized (lowercase, no punctuation, parentheticals and suffixes removed) and matched on exact or token containment. ACTIVE = on a working list (excluded). BANK = only in an old research bank (kept, flagged 'Only in an old research bank'). Partial matches reviewed by hand (Virgin Voyages vs Virgin Group, Marriott Vacations vs Marriott International, Wonder Group vs Light & Wonder: different companies, kept).

Five agents on 27-Oct-2026: one Yuno inside view (product docs, y.uno, press, repo, memory; Glean unreachable) and four US sweeps by cluster (travel and mobility; subscriptions, media and software; marketplaces, retail, food, ticketing; gaming, betting, fintech, telco, education). 119 of 200 web searches used, plus unlimited page fetches (10-Ks, PSP customer pages, case studies, privacy policies). Claude then verified the fit 4 and 5 rows directly (see Verification column) and checked storefronts for Shopify (Shop Pay) to apply the own-contracts gate.

5 = four or more signals including multi-PSP or multi-market; 4 = three signals; 3 = two signals with clear volume; 2 = volume but single market, single PSP, Shopify-captive or app-store captive; 1 = does not qualify (not listed). Signals: multiple PSPs or acquirers; 3+ countries; subscriptions or card-on-file at scale; payouts; multi-brand after M&A; manual reconciliation; single-PSP concentration at $500M+; triggers (RFP, new Head of Payments, new CFO, IPO, outage).

Applied to fit 4 and 5 rows only, from the Yuno inside-view checklist: gates (NA decision center; own checkout and PSP contracts; not a PSP, partner or existing customer) then 12 weighted criteria: volume 15, processor plurality or concentration 15, multi-market 12, recurring share 10, reconciliation complexity 10, orchestration status 8, local method gaps 8, triggers 7, vertical margin 5, engineering and PCI drain 5, pain evidence 3, referenceability 2. 75+ = eyes closed; 55 to 74 = strong, lead with the dominant pain; 35 to 54 = narrow, one product entry.

Add to Core ICP now = fit 5, or fit 4 with High confidence (stack or multi-market verified by Claude). Add to Master, research stack = fit 4 with Medium or Low confidence. Keep in bank = fit 3. Skip = fails a gate (Shopify-captive, in-house builder, payments provider, non-US, too small).

Glean was unreachable, so internal ICP docs and the customer list were not checked there. Most processors are undisclosed: a 10-K rarely names them. Revenue figures come from 10-Ks or press as cited; estimates are marked. Bank rows carry German's own mid-2026 research and were not re-verified except where the Verification column says so. The Payments leader column is blank except where an agent found a verifiable name.
